description: 0/0 indeterminate limits at x→0 involving ln(1±kx) type expressions, solved using the standard limit lim_{x→0} ln(1+x)/x = 1.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.technique: Split into ln(1+x)/x and ln(1-x)/(-x), use lim_{u→0} ln(1+u)/u = 1
Split and rescale each term to match the standard limit ln(1+u)/u → 1 as u→0
Split into two fractions, each rescaled to the standard ln(1+u)/u limit
Split numerator, rescale each term to the standard ln(1+u)/u limit
Use sinc limit sin(x)/x → 1 combined with ln(1+u)/u → 1
Rewrite as ln(1+(x^2+2\sin^2 x)) using 1-cos2x = 2sin^2x, then apply ln(1+u)/u → 1
Rewrite as ln(1+(x sin3x + 2sin^2 x)) then apply ln(1+u)/u → 1 with sinc limits
Rewrite as ln(1+2(e^{x^2}-1+\sin^2 2x)) then apply ln(1+u)/u → 1 with exponential and sinc limits
Rewrite as ln(1+(1-e^{-x^2}\cos 2x)) then expand using exponential and sinc standard limits
Rewrite as ln(1+(1-\cos 2x\cos 4x)) then split using 1-cos2x=2sin^2x identities and sinc limits
